result: The authors report that significantly increased numbers of senescent osteoclasts (SnOCs), identified by p16+TRAP+ staining and SA-βGal markers, are observed in mouse models of spinal hypersensitivity (LSI and aging) compared to controls. This represents a novel finding that osteoclasts undergo cellular senescence during injury and aging in the vertebral endplate.
evaluation: Multiple reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. One reviewer states 'they first showed that greater numbers of SnOCs are observed in mouse models of LSI or aging,' and another notes 'a greater number of senescent osteoclasts (SnOCs)...are responsible for innervation in the LSI and aging animal models.' The editor describes this as 'compelling evidence for the SnOCs to induce sensory nerve innervation.'

result: The larger population of SnOCs is associated with induced sensory nerve innervation (CGRP+ PGP9.5+ nerves) and growth of H-type vessels (CD31+Emcn+) in the porous endplate. The authors demonstrate increased expression of nerve growth factors Netrin-1 and NGF in LSI and aged mice.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently affirm this association. One reviewer states 'these SnOCs are associated with induced sensory nerve innervation, as well as the growth of H-type vessels, in the porous endplate.' Another notes the study 'discovered that the clearance of senescent osteoclasts can lead to a reduction in sensory nerve innervation...as well as the regulation of H-type vessels.' The data is described as 'convincing' and 'strongly support[ing] the idea.'

result: Administration of the senolytic drug ABT263 results in significantly reduced spinal hypersensitivity (measured by behavioral tests including PWF, heat response times, distance traveled, and active time), spinal degeneration, endplate porosity, sensory nerve innervation, and H-type vessel growth in both LSI and aged mouse models.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly support these findings. One reviewer states 'the deletion of senescent cells by administration of the senolytic drug Navitoclax (ABT263) results in significantly less spinal hypersensitivity, spinal degeneration, porosity of the endplate, sensory nerve innervation, and H-type vessel growth.' The editor notes 'reduction of SnOCs by the senolytic drug Navitoclax markedly reduces spinal pain sensitivity.' Reviewers describe the experiments as 'well-designed' with 'rigorous data.'

result: SnOCs exhibit significantly increased secretion of Netrin-1 and NGF, two well-established sensory nerve growth factors, compared to non-senescent osteoclasts. The authors conclude that SnOCs mediate nerve fiber innervation through elevated secretion of these neurotrophic factors.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. One reviewer states 'they also found that there is greater SnOC-mediated secretion of Netrin-1 and NGF, two well-established sensory nerve growth factors, compared to non-senescent OCs.' Another notes 'a greater number of senescent osteoclasts (SnOCs), which produce Netrin-1 and NGF, are responsible for innervation.' One reviewer specifically highlights this as showing 'for the first time...that SnOCs promote LBP by neurotrophic-mediated pathways.'

result: ABT263 treatment significantly reduces endplate porosity, trabecular bone separation (Tb.Sp), endplate degeneration scores, distribution of MMP13 and ColX, and TRAP+ osteoclast numbers in both aged and LSI mouse models, demonstrating a pivotal role in mitigating spinal degeneration and maintaining endplate remodeling.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm these structural and histological findings as part of the overall therapeutic effect. One reviewer notes the study shows ABT263 'results in significantly less...spinal degeneration, porosity of the endplate.' Another states 'the IVD structure was restored by treatment with ABT263.' The data is described as 'convincing' and the study as 'well conducted.'

result: ABT263 treatment significantly mitigates the aberrant innervation of sensory nerves and blood vessels within the endplate in LSI and aged mouse models, effectively reducing spinal hypersensitivity by diminishing this innervation.
evaluation: Reviewers support this mechanistic conclusion. One reviewer states the study shows 'clearance of senescent osteoclasts can lead to a reduction in sensory nerve innervation...resulting in a decrease in pain-related behavior.' Another notes the 'logic is clear and clarifies the pathological role of SnOCs.' The editor describes the evidence as 'compelling.'

result: The authors suggest that pharmacological elimination of SnOCs, perhaps by use of a senolytic drug, may be a potent therapy to treat spinal pain and represents a new avenue in the management of this widespread condition.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm the therapeutic potential. One reviewer states 'their findings represent a potential treatment for spine pain utilizing senolytic drugs.' Another notes the study 'suggest[s] the potential utilization of senolytic drugs for the treatment of LBP.' The editor states 'this work will be of broad interest to regenerative biologists working on spinal pain.' While speculative, reviewers treat this conclusion as well-supported by the data.

result: LSI and aged mouse models exhibit significantly reduced active time, distance traveled, maximum speeds, heat response times, and increased paw withdrawal frequency compared to sham controls, along with increased endplate porosity and trabecular bone separation measured by μCT.
evaluation: Reviewers implicitly accept these baseline characterizations of the disease models as part of the overall study design. One reviewer notes 'the experiments are well-designed' and another states 'the study is well conducted and data strongly support the idea.' No concerns are raised about the model characterization.

result: The authors acknowledge that ABT263 does not specifically eliminate SnOCs and that further studies are required to prove the role of SnOCs in spinal hypersensitivity. They also note that ABT263 possesses various on-target and/or off-target toxicities that could preclude its clinical use.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these acknowledged limitations. All reviewers state 'all my concerns have been well addressed, no further comments' or provide no critique of these limitations, suggesting implicit acceptance of the authors' acknowledgment of study constraints.
